answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 53% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the garden calculation reruns each epoch, the jetty weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the dawn settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 114 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 21 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
